subject: critical_thinking
question: Amnesty International (AI), a non-governmental organisation for the protection of human rights enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, opposes the death penalty. Which one of the following reasons for opposing the death penalty is inconsistent with the principles of AI.

choices.A: The death penalty can be carried out on an innocent person.
choices.B: The death penalty is contrary to theological principles.
choices.C: The death penalty is cruel, inhuman and degrading.
choices.D: The death penalty is not a deterrent against crime.
choices.E: The death penalty, once carried out, cannot be reversed.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Three red balls, three yellow balls and one green ball are placed in a bag and the bag is shaken. I place my hand in the bag and pull out a red ball followed by a green ball. I do not replace either ball. Which one of the following statements is true?

choices.A: The next ball could be any one of red, yellow or green.
choices.B: The next ball will definitely be yellow.
choices.C: The next two balls cannot both be red.
choices.D: At least one of the next three balls must be yellow.
choices.E: At least one of the next three balls must be red.

subject: critical_thinking
question:
My friend has three children, Alice, George and Hannah and I need to buy two presents for them to share. I want to buy two different toys and I want to make sure that Alice, George and Hannah will each like at least one of them. I don't want the toys to have small parts.
[Toy | Small Parts? | Liked by Alice? | Liked by George? | Liked by Hannah? | Price]
Jigsaw | Yes | No | Yes | Yes | 12
Building bricks | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | 9
Car | No | No | No | Yes | 12
Bear | No | Yes | No | Yes | 7
Train | No | No | Yes | No | 8
How much am I going to pay in total?

subject: critical_thinking
question: Two security guards, Dave and Geoff, are patrolling an airbase. Dave passes the front gate every 8 minutes. Geoff passes the front gate every 15 minutes. They have just set off on their individual routes at the start of their shift. How long will it be before they meet up at the front gate again?

choices.A: 1h 00mins
choices.B: 1h 30mins
choices.C: 2h 00mins
choices.D: 2h 30mins
choices.E: 3h 00mins

subject: critical_thinking
question:
Employees at a printing company are paid a basic rate of 11 euro per hour during the day Monday to Friday. During weekday evenings and on Saturdays they are paid at one and a half times the basic rate and on Sundays they are paid at double the basic rate. The table below shows the hours worked by employees last week:
[Employee | Mon-Fri daytime | Mon-Fri evenings and Saturdays | Sundays]
Alice | 32 | 8 | 6
Ben | 27 | 8 | 8
Chetan | 36 | 8 | 2
Daniel | 30 | 8 | 6
Ellen | 35 | 8 | 4
Which employee earned most last week?

choices.A: Alice
choices.B: Ben
choices.C: Chetan
choices.D: Daniel
choices.E: Ellen

subject: critical_thinking
critical_thinking
question: It has long been thought that birds are much less intelligent than humans and apes. But now it seems that some species of birds have the same kind of thinking skills as apes. Crows can create and use tools and are socially sophisticated when finding and protecting food. So how can a bird with a walnut-size brain be capable of such achievements? The answer is that both crows and apes have much bigger brains than you would expect from the size of their bodies. The same pattern is found in humans, parrots and chimps - all intelligent animals. Which one of the following can be drawn as a conclusion from the above passage?

choices.A: Apes are not as similar to humans as had been thought.
choices.B: Crows are more intelligent than other species of birds.
choices.C: Animals that cannot create tools are not intelligent.
choices.D: Relative brain size is a better indicator of intelligence than absolute brain size.
choices.E: It could be argued that birds are as intelligent as apes.

subject: critical_thinking
question: There is a higher than average risk of death or injury to young drivers and their passengers. In 2007, 32 per cent of car driver deaths and 40 per cent of car passenger deaths were people aged between 17 and 24. Young male drivers were much more likely to be killed or seriously injured than young female drivers. So in order to reduce the number of road accidents and the numbers of people killed or injured, young people should not be allowed to drive until they reach the age of 24. Which one of the following is an assumption on which this argument depends?

choices.A: Young people would not accept the raising of the legal driving age.
choices.B: Most of the accidents involving young people were the fault of the young drivers.
choices.C: The driving test does not effectively test the skill of drivers.
choices.D: The majority of drivers aged between 17 and 24 drive dangerously.
choices.E: Amongst drivers aged between 17 and 24 there are more male drivers than female drivers.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Some disabled people find it difficult to gain access to some of our older public buildings because the entrances have steps. The problem is most often solved by installing ramps. All public buildings must be accessible to everyone therefore they must all install ramps. Which one of the following identifies the flaw in this argument?

choices.A: Disabled people must have access to all buildings not just public ones so all buildings should have ramps.
choices.B: Installing ramps in all public buildings would be extremely expensive.
choices.C: It is unreasonable to suggest that disabled people should be able to access all public buildings.
choices.D: Some older public buildings without ramps may be accessible to disabled people.
choices.E: Inaccessible public buildings should be replaced by buildings accessible to all.

subject: critical_thinking
question: A street of houses is numbered starting on one side with 1,2,3,4.... At the far end the numbers continue down the other side in the opposite direction so the largest number is opposite number 1. The houses are of identical widths so each house has another directly opposite it. If number 17 is directly opposite number 56, how many houses are there in the street?

subject: critical_thinking
question:
A courier starts the day in London and makes two round trips to Prague in the day. When she arrives at either airport, she takes the next available flight back. The daily timetable is shown below (all times are local):
[London depart | Prague arrive | Prague depart | London arrive]
06:30 | 09:30 | 10:10 | 11:20
09:45 | 12:45 | 13:25 | 14:35
12:30 | 15:30 | 16:40 | 17:50
15:45 | 18:45 | 19:55 | 21:05
How long is the courier's day from first take-off to last landing?

choices.A: 4 hours 50 minutes
choices.B: 8 hours 5 minutes
choices.C: 8 hours 20 minutes
choices.D: 11 hours 20 minutes
choices.E: 14 hours 35 minutes

subject: critical_thinking
question:
My three local supermarkets all currently have offers on my favourite breakfast cereal as follows:
1 Buy one standard pack get a second half price.
2 Price of a standard pack reduced by 1/3.
3 Normal price of a standard pack, pack contains 25% extra.
Which of the offers are equivalent in terms of price per unit amount of cereal?

choices.A: 1 and 2 only
choices.B: 1 and 3 only
choices.C: 2 and 3 only
choices.D: 1, 2 and 3
choices.E: none

subject: critical_thinking
question: If the Carnival Committee does not follow the new European regulations then it may be impossible to guarantee safety. The probable consequence of this would be a heavy fine, which would severely reduce the carnival fund, and could be disastrous for the committee's finances. Either the committee must meet the safety requirements or the future of the carnival may be under threat. Which one of the following best expresses the conclusion of this argument?

choices.A: Safety at the carnival has reached dangerously low levels.
choices.B: If the European regulations are not followed the carnival may not survive.
choices.C: Failure to improve safety could result in a heavy fine.
choices.D: A heavy fine could mean financial disaster for the carnival.
choices.E: If the regulations are followed then the carnival will take place again next year.

subject: critical_thinking
question: 87% of the world population are right-handed. The human world is organised to make success in life easier for the majority. Left-handed people should therefore be considered as having a disability and receive appropriate support. Which one of the following, if true, weakens this argument?

choices.A: Amongst top scientists, sportsmen, actors, musicians and politicians the percentage of left-handed people is much higher than 13%.
choices.B: Left-handed people have poorer spatial skills which makes them more likely to have car crashes and other serious accidents.
choices.C: Left-handed people are more likely to have health problems such as allergies, depression, epilepsy and sleeping disorders.
choices.D: Hand tools, musical instruments and scissors are designed for use by the majority.
choices.E: Many left-handed people were forced to write with their right hand when they were at school.

subject: critical_thinking
question: In North America in the 1800s, arguments were often settled by gunfights, in which two people stood face to face a distance apart and tried to shoot one another. Recent experiments on human response times have shown that people act more quickly when responding to an action than when they are the first to move. This supports the view that our brain uses different routes in our nervous system to send messages for intentional and reactive movements. Which one of the following can be drawn as a conclusion from the above passage?

choices.A: Scientific experiments produce interesting findings.
choices.B: Gunfighters are best advised to wait for their opponents to move to fire.
choices.C: Gunfighters who wait for their opponent to move first would always win.
choices.D: Brains cannot control our reactive movements.
choices.E: Humans can be trained to react more quickly.

subject: critical_thinking
question: A taxi driver charges 1.00 euro per kilometre for the first 3 kilometres of a journey, and 70c per kilometre for the rest of the journey. I travel home from the train station by taxi. I pay the taxi driver 10.00 euro including a tip of 70c. How far is my house from the station?

choices.A: 9 kilometres
choices.B: 10 kilometres
choices.C: 12 kilometres
choices.D: 13 kilometres
choices.E: 14 kilometres

subject: critical_thinking
question:
The table below relates to electricity generation in the United Kingdom:
[Category of Station | 1990 | 1995 | 2000] (Millions of units, kWh)
Coal, Oil and Gas | 242,300 | 228,500 | 245,700
Nuclear | 37,000 | 61,100 | 65,700
Gas Turbines and Oil Engines | 500 | 1,100 | 400
Hydro-Electric (Natural Flow) | 3,900 | 4,100 | 5,100
Hydro-Electric (Pumped Storage) | 1,200 | 2,800 | 2,000
TOTAL | 284,900 | 297,600 | 318,900
Which category of station made the largest contribution to the increase in total units generated over the 10 years covered by the table?

choices.A: Coal, Oil and Gas
choices.B: Nuclear
choices.C: Gas Turbines and Oil Engines
choices.D: Hydro-Electric (Natural Flow)
choices.E: Hydro-Electric (Pumped Storage)

subject: critical_thinking
question: If more workers worked for only four days each week there would be fewer commuters, and therefore less traffic congestion and less pollution. Also, fewer people would be unemployed because there would be more work to go around. There is evidence that part-time workers are absent from work less often than full-time workers, so a person working a four-day week would be more productive. Less work means less pressure, which means less stress and people would be happier. Which one of the following can be drawn as a conclusion from the above passage?

choices.A: People choosing to work a four-day week would have to take a 20% pay cut.
choices.B: There would be less pressure on the health services if most workers were on a four-day week.
choices.C: The economy would be more competitive if people worked more productively.
choices.D: The government should enforce a four-day working week.
choices.E: There would be many benefits to working a four-day week.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Migratory birds which are unable to fly long distances without resting have to use the shortest distance over water in their flights to and from Africa, and so they cross at the Straits of Gibraltar. It is essential for these birds, some of which are very rare, that the route remains open. For that reason, it is important that plans to build electricity-generating wind farms on the hills surrounding the Straits of Gibraltar do not go ahead. Which one of the following is an assumption on which this argument depends?

choices.A: The birds that migrate across the Straits of Gibraltar are close to extinction.
choices.B: Electricity-generating wind farms have to be built on hills.
choices.C: The planned wind farms will make it dangerous for migratory birds to use their route.
choices.D: Other species of bird can fly further and can thus use other routes in their migration.
choices.E: There are no plans to build wind farms at other places along the coast.

subject: critical_thinking
question: When mobile phones were introduced there were concerns about the microwaves produced and the effects that these could have on the brain, given that phones would be held close to the ear when being used. These concerns have been shown to be mistaken since mobile phones are used for sending text messages far more than for making phone calls. Sending a text message does not require the phone to be anywhere near to the brain so it cannot cause any problems. Which one of the following identifies the flaw in this argument?

choices.A: It ignores research showing that microwaves from the phones cannot penetrate far enough to reach the brain.
choices.B: It ignores evidence suggesting that text messaging is only popular in certain age groups.
choices.C: It does not consider uses of mobile phones other than making phone calls and sending text messages.
choices.D: It does not consider other technology such as wireless internet which could cause similar problems.
choices.E: It ignores the possible effects of the phone calls that are made.

subject: critical_thinking
question: I have two cousins. One was born the year before me, on June 3rd. The other was born the year after me, on April 28th. My birthday is May 15th. For how many days each year am I the same age as one or other of my cousins?

subject: critical_thinking
question:
The table shows the number of people aged 20-35, 36-50 and 51-65 who participated in given sports at a leisure centre on a Sunday morning:
[Sport | 20-35 | 36-50 | 51-65]
Swimming | 31 | 42 | 59
Squash | 26 | 30 | 44
Aerobics | 10 | 21 | 30
Tennis | 40 | 35 | 32
Bowls | 6 | 8 | 11
Table Tennis | 28 | 32 | 46
In which of the other sports was the proportion of participants in the three age ranges closest to that for swimming?

choices.A: Aerobics
choices.B: Bowls
choices.C: Squash
choices.D: Table Tennis
choices.E: Tennis

subject: critical_thinking
question:
Apples cost 30c each, bananas cost 40c each and oranges cost 50c each. Daniel spends exactly 2 euro buying fruit. Which of the statements below are correct?
1 He cannot have exactly 3 apples.
2 He must have at least one banana.
3 He has 4, 5 or 6 fruits.
4 If he has all 3 types of fruit, he must have fewer apples than bananas and oranges combined.

choices.A: 1, 2 and 3 only
choices.B: 1, 2 and 4 only
choices.C: 1, 3 and 4 only
choices.D: 2, 3 and 4 only

subject: critical_thinking
question: A comparison has been made between fast food restaurants and factories. This is not as unrealistic as it might first appear. Fast food is mass-produced, as heavily processed as any other factory product, and restaurant workers have jobs which are just as routine and boring as those in manufacturing. So not only does fast food taste the same everywhere, but all workers involved are on low wages and have little power to improve their conditions. Which one of the following best expresses the conclusion of this argument?

choices.A: Workers who do routine and boring jobs are often poorly paid.
choices.B: Mass production in factories leads to poor working conditions.
choices.C: It is not unrealistic to compare fast food restaurants with factories.
choices.D: All fast food tastes the same because it is heavily processed.
choices.E: Working in a fast food restaurant is no different from working in a factory.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Recent research suggests that people are becoming less inclined to follow medical advice about how to prevent ill-health. They say that there is too much advice and it is often contradictory. However the general population is living longer and is healthier. This suggests that people are more aware of what is good for their own health and wellbeing than the medical profession is. Which one of the following, if true, weakens this argument?

choices.A: Advances in medicine have meant that doctors give advice on a wider range of issues.
choices.B: People now have easy access to websites giving information on health.
choices.C: People believe that they know better than doctors how to improve their own health and wellbeing.
choices.D: The health improvements are in areas that exactly match the medical advice given by doctors.
choices.E: Doctors prefer to give advice rather than medication.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Over the last twenty years the number of people, including children, classed as overweight, and therefore at risk of serious health problems, has risen alarmingly. This trend could be caused by an increase in the amount people eat or by a decrease in the amount of exercise they take. Most of us exercise less than people did twenty years ago, and the average number of calories consumed per person is now less than it was twenty years ago. So the increase in the number of overweight people is clearly caused by lack of exercise. Thus the government does not need to worry about trying to change people's diets. Which one of the following identifies the flaw in this argument?

choices.A: Some people may exercise more than the average.
choices.B: Some individuals may have increased their calorie intake.
choices.C: The government may need to worry about costs to the health service.
choices.D: Children may use up more calories through exercise than adults.
choices.E: Some individuals may have health problems which cause an increase in weight.

subject: critical_thinking
question: In 2005, Peter's age was exactly four times that of his son, Quentin. In 2021, Peter will be exactly twice Quentin's age. What is the difference between their ages?

subject: critical_thinking
question: I have far too much small change in my pocket: 6 x 1c coins, 3 x 2c coins, 2 x 5c coins, 3 x 10c coins and 2 x 50c coins. I want to buy a chocolate bar for 37c using as many coins as possible. What is the largest number of coins I can use to pay the exact price?

subject: critical_thinking
question:
A fishing club wishes to send out a mailing to its 1000 members. All members receive a magazine (100 g). There are 50 committee members who receive minutes (50 g). A questionnaire (75 g) will be sent to 100 members. No committee members will be sent a questionnaire. The envelope used for all mailings weighs 10 g.
The postal rates are:
Up to 120g: 20c
Up to 160g: 30c
Up to 250g: 35c
What is the minimum cost of this mailing?

choices.A: 67.00 euro
choices.B: 215.00 euro
choices.C: 220.00 euro
choices.D: 230.00 euro
choices.E: 350.00 euro

subject: critical_thinking
question: The general public cannot understand laws and legal documents unless they are written in clear and simple language. Therefore, the traditional style in which laws and legal documents are written must change. Citizens in a democracy must be able to understand what their legal rights and duties are. Which one of the following best expresses the conclusion of this argument?

choices.A: There must be a change in the style in which laws and legal documents are written.
choices.B: It is necessary in a democracy for citizens to know their legal rights and duties.
choices.C: Many laws and legal documents are written in old-fashioned and complicated language.
choices.D: The general public can fully understand only those laws and documents written in simple language.
choices.E: If citizens can understand laws and legal documents, they will be able to play their proper role in a democracy.

subject: critical_thinking
question: Many countries spent billions on vaccines in response to advice that a virus had the potential to kill millions. These countries are now trying to sell the stockpiles of vaccines which they do not need. There is concern that advice given by officials may have been influenced by pharmaceutical companies. Clearly, such companies would have an interest in making sure that governments spent large quantities of money on vaccines that they produced. It is essential that an investigation into this matter takes place as soon as possible so that those responsible can be held to account. Which one of the following is an assumption on which this argument depends?

choices.A: The pharmaceutical companies influenced the advice given by officials.
choices.B: The advice given by officials was not appropriate.
choices.C: It will not be possible for the stockpiles of vaccines to be sold.
choices.D: The pharmaceutical companies misjudged the dangers of the virus.
choices.E: Groups with financial interests do not advise officials in other areas of decision making.

subject: critical_thinking
question:
Consider the following statements:
1 There are fewer rats than people.
2 There are not more people than rats.
3 There are at least as many rats as people.
4 There are not more rats than people.
Which two of the above statements are equivalent?

choices.A: 1 and 3
choices.B: 1 and 4
choices.C: 2 and 3
choices.D: 2 and 4
choices.E: 3 and 4
